text:
The Toronto Maple Leafs got a point on Thursday, their first since Halloween. That's the good news. The rest of it: they led the Los Angeles Kings 3-0 early in the second period and lost 4-3 in a shootout, stretching their winless run to eight games (0-7-1).

The start looked like the slump was breaking. Auston Matthews scored on the power play, then set up John Tavares late in the first. Dakota Joshua made it 3-0 at 2:34 of the second.

It lasted almost no time. Alex Turcotte tipped one in at 2:55, Alex Laferriere tipped in a power-play goal at 10:11, and Erik Haula's slap shot at 14:51 tied it, swinging the Kings' win chance from 26% to 48%. Los Angeles carried even strength in the middle of the game and finished with the better five-on-five chances, 2.64 expected goals to 2.16 (expected goals measure the quality of chances). By the full count it was a coin flip: Toronto deserved to win 51% of the time.

Overtime gave Matthews the best look of the night, a 24% chance that Darcy Kuemper stopped, the save that added the most wins of anyone in the game. In the shootout, Adrian Kempe scored in the first round, and Kuemper stopped Matthews, William Nylander and Jack Roslovic.

There was an extra layer behind the benches. Jim Hiller, who coached the Kings before taking the Toronto job in June, faced his old team, now run by Peter Laviolette. Nylander has been taking public criticism this week, and the questions about Matthews' future in Toronto aren't going away. A blown three-goal lead at home is the kind of loss that keeps all of that going, even with a point attached.
headline: Leafs blow a 3-0 lead, winless streak hits eight
